title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing + padding minimization heuristics (v18)
author: Ethan Kim
commits: Initial implementation: seqlen bucketer and pad minimizer
Add unit tests and microbench harness
Integrate kernel cost model for bucket scoring
Fix bucket boundary edge cases and off-by-one
Rollout: add feature flag and gradual rollout logic
changed_files: runtime/scheduler/batcher.py (+120 -32) - implement bucketing and padding optimizer
runtime/scheduler/bucket_selector.cc (+78 -15) - cost model and bucket scorer
runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc (+60 -8) - expose cost estimates per sequence length
runtime/kv_cache/cache.py (+40 -10) - avoid cache thrash on re-bucketing; emit prefix_hit metrics
benchmarks/batching/bench_seqlen.py (+60 -4) - mixed workload harness and baseline scripts
description: Motivation: mixed-seqlen workloads suffer padding waste when continuous batching groups requests with long outliers. This PR implements an adaptive seqlen bucketing and padding-minimization heuristic that reduces average padding while preserving throughput and latency SLOs. Approach: 1) Collect sequence-length distribution online (per-worker, short-time quantiles) and propose candidate bucket boundaries using a cost model that trades padding vs scheduling overhead. 2) For each candidate bucket, estimate per-token kernel cost using an augmented kernel selector; compute expected padding overhead and select buckets that minimize total inferred token cost under a max-bucket-count constraint. 3) At runtime, the batcher places incoming requests into buckets and only pads within-bucket to the bucket max, with an allowed slack parameter to absorb small length variance and avoid excessive fragmentation. 4) Integrations: a) kernel selector exposes cost estimates for sequences to score buckets; b) scheduler backpressure logic updated to prefer filling existing buckets before opening new ones; c) KV cache touch logic adjusted so re-bucketing does not evict hot KV entries unnecessarily and prefix-hit metrics added to detect adverse cache churn. Rollout: guarded by feature flag dynamic_batching_v18 with gradual rollout to 10/30/100% through our rollout service; opt-out for Dedicated customers. Results: microbench on mixed web-chat workload (seqlen distribution 8/32/128) shows +12% throughput and ~8-15% token-cost reduction depending on model/quantization; p95 latency change within +5ms on average and tail stable. Testing: unit and property tests added for bucket assignment and pad minimizer; benchmark harness and CI jobs validate regressions; stress tests on internal perf-canary show no increase in error rate. Observability: new metrics (batch_bucket_counts, pad_overhead_tokens, prefix_kv_hit_rate) and dashboard panels added; alerts tuned to detect increased pad overhead or KV churn. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when feature flag is off; documented migration steps. This PR is the iterative v18 of heuristics after multiple tuning rounds and benchmark runs; includes cleanup of previous v17 flags and finalizes telemetry. Checklist: ensure rollout flag set to false in main, add dedicated opt-out, confirm docs published, run canary for 48h before 100% rollout.
review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice work, clear improvements. Please add a short note in the RFC explaining how slack is chosen and why we don't micro-bucket for every distinct length.
Ethan Kim: Added explanation and tuned slack default to 5 tokens; rationale in RFC section 3.2.
Priya Patel: Can you quantify KV churn impact? I see adjustments to cache touches but would like a short benchmark on prefix hit rates.
Ethan Kim: Added bench that measures prefix_kv_hit_rate; we observe <1% drop and overall token cost improvement outweighs it. Included metric in telemetry dashboard.
Liam Murphy: CI flake on test_heuristics was transient; re-run fixed it. Approving after CI green.
Ava Chen: Approval after small nits addressed (typo in docs).
release_notes: Adaptive dynamic batching by sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization. Estimated throughput improvement ~10-15% on mixed-length workloads and reduced token padding costs. Adds telemetry, rollout flag, and Dedicated opt-out.
